newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Straits buys Dominion out of Whim Creek.
newsitem.headline: Straits buys Dominion out of Whim Creek.

text.p: Straits Resources Ltd said on Tuesday that it would move to full control of the Whim Creek copper project in Western Australia after reaching an agreement to buy the 40 percent stake from Dominion Mining Ltd.
The company said it would pay Dominion A$4 million within 28 days and a further amount of between A$1.5 million and A$3.5 million depending on copper prices in 12 instalments from January 1998.
Whim Creek is located midway between Karratha and Port Hedland and comprises two deposits, Whim Creek and Mons Cupri.
Straits said full ownership would clear the way for an early development decision.
It said Whim Creek was forecast to produce 10,000 tonnes annually of copper cathode, doubling Straits' copper output to 20,000 tonnes and doubling copper revenue to A$67 million.
The company had been earning a 60 percent interest by contributing A$5 million to project exploration and development.
